defects.description: Key hashing is implemented ad hoc as _key_hash (HMAC-SHA256) in the route module authsvc/routes/api_keys.py, and principal.py imports _key_hash from that route module. This bypasses authsvc/security/hashing.py, whose docstring makes it the single place all stored secrets are hashed (recovery.py follows it), and makes the auth layer depend on a routes module.

The key hash is an HMAC keyed with settings.jwt_secret, reusing the JWT signing key for a second purpose. Rotating JWT_SECRET silently invalidates every stored API key hash, and a JWT key leak also enables offline checking of key hashes. settings.py already has a dedicated secret_pepper for keyed secret hashing that the plan does not use.

The lookup cache TTL is settings.cache_ttl_seconds, whose default (CACHE_TTL_SECONDS) in settings.py is 300 s, and revocation only pops the entry on the instance that served the DELETE. A revoked key therefore keeps authenticating on the other instances for up to 5 minutes, violating R4/AC3 (401 within 60 s on every instance).
defects.location: plan.md steps 6 and 8; fixture/authsvc/settings.py cache_ttl_seconds default; spec.md R4, AC3

defects.description: The plan adds the cachetools dependency and a new TTLCache instead of reusing the existing in-process cache helper authsvc/cache.py TTLMemo (already used by orgs.is_active, which the plan's own step 7 calls).
defects.location: plan.md step 8 and rollout notes; fixture/authsvc/cache.py; fixture/authsvc/orgs.py

defects.description: The existing RequestLogMiddleware (authsvc/reqlog.py) logs the Authorization header at DEBUG through _redact_bearer, which only masks the part after the last '.' (the JWT signature) and returns dotless values unchanged. sk_live_ keys contain no '.', so the full secret is logged at DEBUG, and the rollout runs a canary at LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG. The plan never updates the redaction, violating AC4 and the never-log-secrets constraint.

Audit metadata for api_key.created and api_key.revoked is nested under the field name "api_key", which is in audit.SENSITIVE_KEYS, so scrub() drops the whole object and the audit rows persist empty metadata with no key id, name or scopes. R6 is not met.
defects.location: plan.md steps 4 and 6; fixture/authsvc/audit.py SENSITIVE_KEYS/scrub; spec.md R6

defects.description: The test strategy has no test for AC3 (revoked key rejected within 61 s on every instance; the revoke test only checks the same process), AC5 (1,000 requests in a minute cause at most one last_used_at write), or AC4 (no secret in DB, audit table or logs). The audit test checks action/actor/target but not metadata contents.

The last_used_at UPDATE condition `last_used_at < now() - interval '1 minute'` is NULL (not true) for a key that has never been used, because last_used_at is nullable with no default (step 1). The first write never happens, so last_used_at stays NULL forever and R5 is never satisfied. Needs `last_used_at IS NULL OR ...`.

tensions.description: Architecture's natural fix is to route API key hashing through security/hashing.py's hash_secret/verify_secret, which the module docstring says every stored secret must use. Those are argon2 with parameters from settings.argon2_params() (time_cost 3, 64 MiB, parallelism 2), tens of milliseconds and 64 MiB per call. Verifying on every request at about 333 rps per instance blows the spec's 5 ms p95 budget and turns random sk_live_ tokens into a cheap CPU/memory DoS. Risk's natural fix keeps a fast HMAC but switches the key to secret_pepper, which leaves hashing outside the one-hashing-module convention. The argon2 cost is only visible in settings.py plus the spec NFR, and the convention only in hashing.py.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Delete the inline _key_hash and hash/verify API keys with security.hashing.hash_secret / verify_secret like every other stored secret.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Keep a fast HMAC-SHA256 for the high-entropy keys but key it with settings.secret_pepper instead of jwt_secret (with compare_digest).
tensions.reconciliation: Add a fast keyed helper (e.g. hash_api_key / verify_api_key: HMAC-SHA256 with settings.secret_pepper, hmac.compare_digest) to security/hashing.py next to the argon2 functions, documenting that high-entropy machine keys use a keyed fast hash because argon2's per-call cost can't meet the 5 ms per-request budget. Both routes/api_keys.py and principal.py import it from security/hashing.py (no principal->routes import). Argon2 stays for passwords and recovery codes.

tensions.description: Consistency's natural fix for the revocation window is to cap the key cache TTL at 60 s or less instead of the 300 s CACHE_TTL_SECONDS default. Architecture's natural fix is to drop cachetools and reuse authsvc/cache.py TTLMemo. Combined as written (TTLMemo(ttl=30)), it fails: TTLMemo defaults to refresh_on_hit=True, so every cache hit pushes the entry's expiry forward. A key in continuous use (exactly the CI keys this feature is for) never expires on instances that didn't serve the DELETE, so a revoked hot key keeps working indefinitely and AC3 still fails. The sliding-expiry default is only visible in cache.py; the 60 s cross-instance bound is only in the spec plus the settings default.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Set the API key cache TTL to 60 s or less (e.g. 30 s) instead of the shared 300 s cache_ttl_seconds default.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Replace the new cachetools TTLCache (and the new dependency) with the existing authsvc.cache.TTLMemo.
tensions.reconciliation: Reuse TTLMemo but construct it with refresh_on_hit=False (absolute expiry from load time) and a dedicated TTL of 30 s or less, not the shared CACHE_TTL_SECONDS. Keep the local evict on DELETE, drop cachetools, and add a test with an injected clock and two memo instances (two simulated app instances) showing a continuously used revoked key is rejected within 60 s.
